name: Saint Ignatius of Loyola
history: A Basque soldier whose leg was shattered by a cannonball at Pamplona, and who, reading the life of Christ during his long recovery, gave himself to God. From his own experience he wrote the Spiritual Exercises, and with companions from the University of Paris he founded the Society of Jesus. He governed it from Rome until his death.
life: Íñigo López de Loyola was a courtier and soldier who dreamed of glory and of noble ladies. Wounded at Pamplona in 1521, he lay for months at Loyola with nothing to read but a life of Christ and lives of the saints. He noticed that daydreams of worldly fame left him empty, while thoughts of following Christ left him at peace, and from this he learned to discern spirits. At Montserrat he hung his sword before the image of Our Lady, and at Manresa he spent a year in prayer and penance, drafting the Exercises. He went back to school with boys, and at Paris won over companions, among them Francis Xavier and Peter Faber. In 1534 they made vows together at Montmartre, and in 1540 Paul III approved the Society of Jesus. Ignatius spent his last years in Rome writing its constitutions and sending his sons across the world. He died on 31 July 1556.
prayerTo: Saint Ignatius, you learned to find God in all things and to seek His greater glory in everything. Pray for the Society of Jesus, for all who make or give the Exercises, and for me, that I may notice how God moves in my heart, choose what leads me to Him, and give Him my whole self. Amen.
penance: Make the Examen tonight: review the day with God, give thanks, notice where you drew near to Him or away from Him, and ask pardon and help for tomorrow.
meditation: For the greater glory of God: Ignatius asked which of two good things would give God more glory. Ask that of one choice you make today.
prayer: O God, Who, to spread abroad the greater glory of Your name through St. Ignatius, strengthened the Church militant with new power; grant that we who are struggling on earth may, by his help and after his example, be found worthy to be crowned with him in heaven. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
